comment: Extensions ShapeShell will install, and the exact builds it will accept.
This list ships inside the app and is not user-editable: an extension arrives only
through a ShapeShell release, so every entry here is one someone reviewed. Adding a
build means adding its hash and cutting a release, which is deliberate friction.
crxSha256 pins a .crx file's bytes; treeSha256 pins the contents of an unpacked
folder (see allowlist.js hashTree). Both are arrays so an entry can accept more than
one reviewed build, such as an old and a new version during an upgrade.
permissions, optionalPermissions, hostPermissions and contentScriptMatches are the
maximum the manifest may ask for. A manifest asking for anything else is refused.
Optional permissions are listed only so they can be recognised: ShapeShell always
refuses chrome.permissions.request, so they are never actually granted.

extensions.name: Bitwarden Password Manager
extensions.notes: Broad host access is inherent to a password manager: it fills forms on any site, and Onshape sign-in passes through other hosts. Verified working in ShapeShell: login, 2FA, unlock and autofill.

extensions.name: Onshape Drawing Comfort
extensions.notes: GitHub only and 0BSD licensed, so it has no key and no stable extension id; it is pinned by the hash of its files. Dark-mode palettes for the drawing editor. Storage only, and scoped to onshape.com.
